integrator.name: HII Newport News Shipbuilding
integrator.role: hull builder and systems integrator. Not the manufacturer of most major systems
integrator.monopoly: The only US shipyard able to build large-deck nuclear carriers. Every US carrier procured since FY1958 was built there
integrator.method: Modular construction. Sections welded into superlifts, equipment installed while the unit is on the ground, lifted into Dry Dock 12 by a 1,050 metric ton gantry crane
integrator.build_strategy: CVN-79 took modular construction and pre-outfitting to a new level: larger superlifts at a higher state of outfitting completion, more parts installed in shop and on the final assembly platen

systems.system: A1B reactor plant, two per ship
systems.maker: Bechtel Marine Propulsion (design); BWXT (core and fuel)
systems.path: SCN advance procurement, Nuclear Propulsion Equipment, 30 to 72 month lead. Naval Reactors is jointly Navy and DOE

systems.maker: General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems; QinetiQ subcontract

systems.system: Advanced Weapons Elevators, eleven per ship
systems.maker: Federal Equipment Company; MagneMotion linear synchronous motors; Curtiss-Wright Exlar actuators
systems.path: N64498-18-D-4022 engineering and the land-based test site. The single largest driver of this hull's delay
A configuration break from CVN-78's Dual Band Radar. CVN-79 is a different configuration, not a second copy, which weakens any learning-curve comparison between the two hulls

systems.maker: Raytheon Ship Self-Defense System Mk 2 with CEC

systems.path: On CVN-79 this sits inside the GA contract as a subcontract and is invisible at prime level. On CVN-81 it is its own prime, N00019-23-C-0040. The cleanest worked example that the vendor map runs a tier deeper than the contract map
$37,544,972 FPIF mod to 2114, Mar 2024, funded 65% FY2024 SCN and 35% FY2018 SCN

consequences: The two HII contracts buy construction and integration, not content. Electronics, Propulsion Equipment and Ordnance are substantially government furnished, bought on other contracts by other commands.

Neither roll-up method is sufficient alone. A contract roll-up anchored on CAGE 43689 captures the hull and misses the systems. A category roll-up from the P-5 captures the systems but cannot see the contracts beneath them.

Cross-command GFE is where hull attribution breaks. An EMALS shipset bought by NAVAIR on an aviation contract and installed by HII on a NAVSEA ship under a NAVSEA contract has no single line of accounting that says CVN-79 from end to end. That, not the ledger seam, is the hardest attribution problem in this program.
